runs.partial: Partial run: {ran} of the {total} planned gates ran. Not run: {gates}. This verdict covers only the gates that ran.

gates.heading: Gates — run {runId}
gates.notFound: That verification run is no longer available.
gates.loadError: Could not load the verification run: {message}
gates.logOmitted: … (+{count} more lines; run `commandmate verify show {runId}` for the full log)
gates.contractSourceHint: `[contract]` marks a gate the execution contract sent to this branch asked for, rather than one `.commandmate/verify.yaml` declares.

builtin.workEvidence: Work-evidence gate (built-in). Looks for commits ahead of `options.baseRef` or an uncommitted change. With neither, the run is reported as Not started and the remaining gates never run.
builtin.scope: Scope gate (built-in). Reconciles the changed files against the execution contract's `scope.allow` / `scope.deny`. A run with no contract has no scope to judge, so the gate does not run.
builtin.envClean: Env-clean gate (built-in). Compares the machine against the snapshot taken when the task started: listening servers, `mcbd-*` tmux sessions, `$HOME` and `~/.commandmate`.
builtin.config: Config gate (built-in). A pseudo-gate that records why `.commandmate/verify.yaml` could not be read. When it is present, no real gate ran at all.

skipReason.primaryCheckout: This worktree is the server process's own working directory, so `options.skipInPrimaryCheckout` declined the gate. That guard protects the running UI from a mid-flight rebuild — it is not a defect. The gate runs normally in any other worktree.
skipReason.workEvidence: The `work-evidence` gate did not pass, so there was nothing for this gate to judge.
skipReason.mutex: Another verification holding the same `mutex` did not finish within the wait budget, so the command was never started. That is a resource conflict, not a verdict on the work.
skipReason.detachedContract: This branch has an execution contract, but the run was not attached to it, so the declared scope went unjudged. Starting the run with `wait --verify` attaches it automatically.
skipReason.noContract: No execution contract is attached to this run, so no scope is declared to check.
skipReason.notRequired: The execution contract sets `success.requireScopeClean: false`, so the scope was not judged.
skipReason.unknown: This gate did not execute. Its log tail says why.
skipReason.cancelled: The verification run was stopped, so this gate reached no verdict. That is the result of stopping the run, not a judgement about the work.

gates.fullLogStored: The server stores only the tail of each gate’s output, capped by `options.maxLogTailBytes`. What you see here is all of it — nothing earlier was kept anywhere.

runStatusGloss.running: Gates are still running; there is no verdict yet.
runStatusGloss.failed: At least one gate failed, timed out, or errored.
runStatusGloss.not_started: No work evidence: neither a commit nor an uncommitted change. There was nothing to judge, so the remaining gates never ran.
runStatusGloss.error: No verdict was reached — gates were left unrun, or the verification config could not be read. This is not the same as failing.
runStatusGloss.cancelled: The run was cancelled before it reached a verdict.

gateStatusGloss.failed: The command exited with a non-zero code.
gateStatusGloss.timeout: The command was cut off before it finished within timeoutSec.
gateStatusGloss.skipped: This gate never executed. That is not the same as passing.
gateStatusGloss.error: The gate could not be started, so it reached no verdict.

chip.noTask: No execution contract has been sent to this branch

selection.heading: Gates to run
selection.hint: Only the selected gates run, so confirming a one-line `lint` fix no longer means waiting for `build` and `unit`. The verdict then covers only the gates that ran, and a narrowed run is labelled as a partial run in the gate table. When the execution contract declares `success.requireWorkEvidence` / `requireScopeClean`, `work-evidence` and `scope` run regardless of the selection — narrowing the gate list cannot drop a criterion the contract declared.
selection.failedOnlyEmpty: The run on screen has no failing gate to re-run. A gate that did not run would simply not run again for the same reason.

commandLabel.wait: Wait for the turn to end

commandDescription.send: Replace the placeholder with your own text. It is left as a placeholder on purpose: quoting a real body — newlines, quotes, non-ASCII — correctly for your shell is not something this page can do without silently truncating it.
commandDescription.wait: Blocks until the agent finishes its turn.
commandDescription.capture: Prints what the agent's pane shows right now. Add --json for a machine-readable form.
commandDescription.respond: Sends the answer to an open prompt. Replace 1 with the number of the option you want.

cliCommands.copyFailed: Could not copy the command. Select the command shown here and copy it manually.
cliCommands.portHint: This server listens on port {port}, so the commands carry a CM_PORT= prefix. These commands have no --port flag; the environment variable is how one invocation is aimed at a non-default server.
cliCommands.noteInstanceFlag: --instance is how a command names its target. --agent is only for starting an ad-hoc session the roster does not know, and wait has no --agent at all.
cliCommands.noteWaitOnPrompt: wait carries --on-prompt human so it keeps waiting when the agent asks something. Without it the default (agent) exits 10 the moment a prompt is detected.
cliCommands.noteRespondNumber: respond does not interpret its answer. Send the NUMBER of the option: "yes" is typed, ignored, and followed by Enter, which picks whatever the default option happens to be.
